newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIA ALLOWS STERLITE TO REOPEN SMELTER.
newsitem.headline: INDIA ALLOWS STERLITE TO REOPEN SMELTER.

text.p: The chief minister of India's southern state of Tamil Nadu said on Wednesday that Sterlite Industries Ltd has been allowed to reopen its copper smelter, closed in July following a suspected gas leak.
"We have decided to allow Sterlite to reopen the copper smelting plant," chief minister M. Karunanidhi told reporters.
"We have imposed certain conditions," Karunanidhi said. "These will be explained in the government order which will be issued later in the day." He did not elaborate.

The state government's decision followed a report by a committee of experts which cleared Sterlite of the charge that its copper smelter pits were behind the suspected gas leak and recommended that the plant be reopened.
In their report released on Tuesday night, the experts said there had been no leak of sulphur dioxide from the 100,000-tonne annual capacity plant based at the port town of Tuticorin.
"Sterlite Industries had been operating within the parameters and conditions prescribed by the state pollution control board," said the report.
The four experts in pollution control and medicine advised Sterlite to take steps to lower its emission levels and sulphur dioxide concentration.
Last month, Sterlite was asked to close down the smelter after suspected gas emissions affected more than 100 workers in a nearby factory.
The report by the experts said that if a gas leak had occurred at the smelter, it would first have affected Sterlite employees before spreading to nearby factories.
Sterlite has strongly denied any leak.
The state's environment minister, N.K.K. Periasamy, on Tuesday said authorities would now investigate if the gas had leaked from any other neighbouring factory.
Sterlite operates India's only private-sector copper smelter, which began production in December 1996.
Company officials have said the closure was costing the company 25 million rupees ($700,000) a day. ($1=35.7 rupees)
